All done. Summary:

## What was filed

**Board #1 (Trading & Fund)** — 32 issues + 3 umbrella drafts:
- **dstrader** #23–33 (11 issues)
- **dstrader-docker** #17–26 (10 issues)
- **FamilyFund** #56–66 (11 issues; #66 was a retry after a GraphQL EOF — umbrella was patched to link the real URL)

**Board #2 (Remote Control)** — 10 issues + 2 drafts:
- **ai-harness** #17–26 (10 issues)
- `[meta] schedule quarterly memory-bank docs review across all 4 repos`

Each repo has an umbrella draft on its board with a checklist linking all its sub-tickets, so you can see the cluster at a glance.

## Pattern picked (from research)

`docs/` folder + root `AGENTS.md` as the agent-readable index (2025/2026 standard, co-promoted by OpenAI/Google/Anthropic/JetBrains); CLAUDE.md becomes a thin pointer. Per-repo docs cover ARCHITECTURE, DATABASE (where applicable), OPERATIONS, DEVELOPMENT, SECURITY, DOMAIN_GLOSSARY, INTEGRATIONS, DECISIONS (ADR index), plus repo-specific subsystem docs. Cline-style `activeContext`/`progress` files were deliberately skipped — they drift when checked in.

## Side notes
- A memory note was saved so future sessions know the cluster exists and to check umbrellas before writing arch docs.
- `GITHUB_PROJECTS.md` still names this repo `dstrader-aws`; actual remote is `dstrader-docker`. Flagged in the dstrader-docker umbrella for ride-along cleanup.

Sources:
- [How to write a great agents.md — GitHub Blog](https://github.blog/ai-and-ml/github-copilot/how-to-write-a-great-agents-md-lessons-from-over-2500-repositories/)
- [AGENTS.md — The File Every AI-Assisted Codebase Should Have](https://medium.com/@satish24sp/agents-md-the-file-every-ai-assisted-codebase-should-have-24490170e765)
- [Cline Memory Bank docs](https://docs.cline.bot/prompting/cline-memory-bank)
- [Effective architecture documentation with arc42 and C4](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/effective-architecture-documentation-arc42-c4-torsten-mosis)
- [Claude Code Memory Management Guide 2026](https://medium.com/data-science-collective/claude-code-memory-management-the-complete-guide-2026-b0df6300c4e8)

**2. Web-research instruction: no, the tickets don't say to research the web.** The current Style block says "1-3 pages, concise, fact-rich, link to code with `path:line` refs, mermaid welcome" — that implicitly biases toward the repo as primary source. Standard frameworks worth consulting (C4 / arc42 for ARCHITECTURE, ADR templates for DECISIONS, STRIDE for SECURITY threat-modeling, finance/trading glossaries) are *not* called out anywhere.

Want me to add a "Research conventions to consult" section? Three sensible scopes:
I'll finish the umbrella patches first, then answer the prefix/label question.

Umbrellas patched. Now to your two questions.

**On prefixes/labels:**
- **Prefixes (in titles):** yes, every ticket. dstrader/dstrader-docker/FamilyFund got `[docs] memory-bank: ...`; ai-harness got `[AH][docs] memory-bank: ...` (matches the existing `[AH]` convention I saw on issues #10–14).
- **GitHub labels:** no. I followed your repos' existing convention of bracket-prefixes in titles rather than GH labels (e.g. `[security][preprod]` on dstrader issues). If you'd rather have a `docs` label too, easy to backfill.

**On launching codex inline to review** — testing now.

**Result: codex CLI is not installed on this Mac.** Not on PATH, not in npm-global, not in homebrew, not in `~/.local/bin`. So I cannot test launching it right now.

The standard install for OpenAI Codex CLI is `npm i -g @openai/codex` (then `codex login`).

Here's the instruction text I'd add to the tickets if we proceed:

```
## After writing the doc — codex review (mandatory)
Run an independent review with the OpenAI Codex CLI (a second model
catches blind spots Claude can miss):

  codex exec --model gpt-5 "Review docs/<NAME>.md against the actual
  repo. Check: (1) factual accuracy — every code reference exists,
  (2) coverage gaps in the scope listed in this ticket, (3) adherence
  to the framework convention (C4 / arc42 / STRIDE / ADR as appropriate),
  (4) drift risk — anything that will rot in 3 months. Output a
  numbered list of specific fixes."

Apply codex's findings (or document why you skipped any) before
marking this ticket Done. If codex CLI is not installed:
  npm i -g @openai/codex && codex login
```
